building.name: 100 First Plaza
building.completed_conflict: The city's Modern & Postmodern styles context statement dates this building 1989; the assessor's roll records it as built 1988.

public_open_space.name: 100 1st St
public_open_space.hours: Ground level arcade space accessible at all times, Sun Terrace open during daylight hours.
public_open_space.location: Sun Terrace is on second floor above adjoining parking garage SE of main building. Ground level arcade is on Mission Street side.
public_open_space.description: The large Sun Terrace features extensive landscaping and seating. Several art sculptures are featured, along with an elevated view of the street below. There is a 'grand' staircase (snippet) up to the Sun Terrace. Ground level arcade in front of building
public_open_space.landscaping: Many trees and plants, water feature, fake grass for sitting.
public_open_space.seating: 52 movable seats at 10 tables plus numerous areas to sit along built-in benches and planters, grassy areas.

public_art.title: Linear Fountain
public_art.art_requirement_note: Predates the 1985 Downtown Plan; the art was provided under approvals guided by the pending plan.
public_art.detail: The water-wall sculpture, made of granite and glass, stands on the Sun Terrace, which also has tiered seating with artificial grass.

historical_record.description: Built as 100 First Plaza, a stepped-back tower clad in granite.
A high-rise built under San Francisco's 1985 Downtown Plan.
112 First Street: a single-storey building whose front was dominated by strong horizontal elements and a large expanse of plate glass. It was cleared for the tower.
104–106 First Street, at Mission: a two-storey rectangular box with a yellow stucco front. It was cleared for the tower.
110 First Street: a five-storey stucco building with moorish detail at its second-floor entablature and panelled spandrels between the floor levels. It was cleared for the tower.

116 First Street: a three-storey building with moorish facade detailing, its third storey articulated by three narrow arched windows divided by bound columns and its cornice carrying a projecting marquee clock. It was cleared for the tower.

118–124 First Street, at Minna: a four-storey rectangular block faced in yellow brick, its second- and third-floor openings recessed with panelled spandrels between the floors. It was cleared for the tower.

511–519 Mission Street: a two-storey stucco building, the oldest of the seven then standing on this block corner, its six-bay front defined at the second level by rusticated piers. It was cleared for the tower.

historic_survey.note: A tower by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill with Heller & Leake, whose pseudo-Art Deco setback top is one of the articulated 'pointy hats' that followed the 1985 Downtown Plan.
